title: egalitarian-slot-allocator-and-deferred-concurrency-limiter-for-dedicated-fleets
author: Evelyn Park
release_notes: Introduces an egalitarian slot allocator and a deferred concurrency limiter for Dedicated fleets to improve fairness across tenants and reduce tail latency during transient contention. See rollout notes for safe gradual enablement.
description: Context: Dedicated fleets occasionally observe localized tenant starvation during short surges when a small number of tenants consume burst capacity in a way that starves steady but latency-sensitive tenants. Motivation: provide a scheduler primitive that enforces proportional minimum throughput guarantees while limiting worst-case tail latency by deferring low-priority concurrency rather than preempting in-flight work. What this PR does: 1) Adds a new EgalitarianSlotAllocator component that tracks per-tenant committed min-slots and a soft pool for ephemeral burst slots. The allocator enforces a refill schedule (configurable window and granularity) and a token decay policy to avoid long-term lock-in. 2) Implements a DeferredConcurrencyLimiter middleware that, when capacity is saturated, queues lower-priority requests into a short-duration holding bucket (configurable 10-200ms) before allowing them to compete for free slots; this reduces in-flight head-of-line blocking and KV-cache pressure. 3) Export new metrics: egalitarian_committed_slots, egalitarian_burst_pool_usage, deferred_limiter_queue_depth, deferred_limiter_requeue_count, and fairness_violation_count. 4) Adds config knobs in the dedicated fleet manifest and Console UI toggles for canary rollout. 5) Includes unit, integration, and perf harness tests plus a stress scenario replay harness used for evaluation. Design notes: The allocator uses a lightweight reservoir accounting algorithm to ensure proportional minimums while allowing best-effort bursts; decays are exponential with a configurable half-life to balance stickiness vs. reclaimability. The deferred limiter operates opportunistically (no guaranteed ordering) to avoid head-of-line amplification and integrates with existing request tracing. Testing & results: In the perf lab run with 400 tenants and a 20% burst cohort, median latency for latency-sensitive tenants improved from 65ms to 42ms and 95th from 310ms to 180ms under identical load; throughput for burst tenants saw a transient 8% reduction in sustained fairness mode. Rollout plan: feature gated behind a config flag; enable by default only in canary fleets for 48 hours, monitor metrics and regressions, then staged enablement 25% -> 50% -> 100% per region. Migration & compatibility: Default behavior is backward-compatible when feature flag is off; config schema includes migration hook to convert legacy per-tenant reservation fields into committed-slot entries. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests and replay harness - [x] Perf runs and artifacts attached - [x] Console toggle implemented - [x] Docs draft added to design RFC - [x] Linear tickets linked (ENG-7351/ENG-7398) Security & safety: limiter ensures no request is dropped silently; deferred timeouts fall back to standard rejection/429 when queue thresholds exceeded. Related: builds on ideas from tenant-fairness RFC and complements headroom controller work. Merge notes: squash-merged with ephemeral commit message "egalitarian slot allocator + deferred concurrency limiter: improve tenant fairness and tail latency".

notes_for_ops: When enabling on production fleets, start in canary for 48h and monitor egalitarian_burst_pool_usage, fairness_violation_count, deferred_limiter_queue_depth, and 95th latency per tenant. If fairness_violation_count spikes, revert flag and run replay harness to capture offending workload. For safety, operator can reduce committed-slot window to shrink commitments immediately.
